caption:
You can now rewrite a website's code by just describing what you want. No coding, no extensions, no GitHub rabbit hole.

Sider Code shipped inside the Sider browser extension on September 1st, and it's the kind of feature that makes you stop scrolling. You type a plain sentence describing how you wish a site worked, and it actually rewrites the live page to make it happen — right there in your browser.

People are already using it to turn a 400-comment Reddit thread into a readable overview, collapse scattered X posts into one clean article with a table of contents, calm down a too-bright site into a dark, quiet workspace, and delete the YouTube Shorts shelf for good. The change sticks too — it saves to that site so it just applies automatically next time you visit.

Worth saying plainly: the code it writes is frozen once applied, so if a site redesigns later, your customization can quietly break. Sider hasn't shipped a way to detect that yet — it's on their roadmap. So think of this as delightfully hacky and personal, not a permanent fix.

Still wild that this is a text box now, not five browser extensions and a GitHub search.

Save this so you remember to try it on the one site that's been annoying you for years. Full breakdown — link in bio.

slides.heading: There's a browser tool that rewrites any website for you
slides.body: You describe the change in plain English. It edits the page's actual code, live, while you watch.

slides.heading: You've done the workaround loop before
slides.body: Hunting GitHub for a userscript, installing five single-purpose extensions, or just living with a site's clutter because coding isn't your thing.

slides.heading: "Summarize this" but for the whole comment section
slides.body: Point it at a sprawling Reddit thread and it restructures hundreds of comments into a clear overview of the actual debate.

slides.heading: Turn a scattered X thread into an article
slides.body: Ask it to rebuild a messy string of posts into a focused article with its own table of contents and navigation.

slides.heading: Tell a bright, cluttered site to calm down
slides.body: It can rewrite a page into a darker, quieter workspace, or make confusing terms explain themselves when you hover over them.

slides.heading: Delete the parts of a site you never asked for
slides.body: Users have removed the YouTube Shorts shelf entirely with one sentence. The fix saves itself and reapplies automatically next visit.

slides.heading: The honest catch: the code is frozen
slides.body: If the site redesigns later, your custom change can silently break, and Sider hasn't shipped a way to detect that yet. It's on their roadmap.

slides.heading: What used to be five extensions is now one sentence
slides.body: No DOM inspector, no coding, no per-site tool. Just describe how the site should work and it does.

slides.heading: One text box replaces the entire workaround habit
slides.body: Reshape comment threads, mute clutter, rebuild messy pages — all from inside the extension you likely already have installed.

slides.heading: Try it on the one site that's annoyed you for years
slides.body: Save this post, open Sider, and describe the fix you've wanted for months. See what changes.
